articles.headline: 49ers DE Romello Height inspired by Patrick Willis to play through broken hand
keyFacts: San Francisco 49ers rookie defensive lineman Romello Height returned to play in Week 4 after undergoing surgery for a broken right hand.
Height said he was inspired by former 49ers linebacker Patrick Willis, who also previously played through a broken hand injury.
Height said he does not know how long he will need to wear the cast during games but will continue playing.
body: A cast is seen on San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Romello Height's (94) hand during his NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. The 49ers defeated the Broncos 24-14. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle)

It's hard to draw many similarities between Romello Height and Patrick Willis. In fact, it'd be foolish to do so. One guy is a rookie defensive end who has played in three NFL games; the other is arguably the greatest linebacker in San Francisco 49ers history.

There is one eerie similarity, however, even if it is born out of pure coincidence: Both players broke their right hands during a game while playing for the 49ers. Both players returned to said game, sporting bulky hard-shelled clubs while in significant pain. And both players went on to miss their first-ever NFL games, each against the Arizona Cardinals, due to the injury.

Height broke his hand early on in the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins. He headed to the locker room and reemerged after halftime with his right hand wrapped in a white cast. In the second half, Height recorded his first NFL sack when he chased Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage.

"I was going off adrenaline," Height said of his second-half performance in the 49ers' 35-13 win. "I felt pain, but it didn't matter at that point. I wanted to play for my brothers, and I wanted to finish the deal."

After further evaluation postgame, doctors determined Height's hand would require surgery. He had a procedure Sept. 22 that kept him out of the 49ers' subsequent contest against the Cardinals, before making his return in Week 4 against the Denver Broncos, starting and playing 37 snaps.

Every time Height dug his right hand into the grass at Levi's Stadium, or wrapped a player up for a tackle, or put a pass-rush move on an offensive lineman, he did so with a swollen right hand that had a large incision just above his index finger.

Protecting his hand was a club - a club so hard that when Height gave fellow rookie Jaden Dugger a fist bump, he questioned how Height was even playing. Beneath his club was "a lot" of protective padding, Height said, giving the cast so much bulk that it could only be compared to a boxing glove.

In 2010, Willis played just three days after undergoing surgery on a broken hand that he suffered during a December game against the Seahawks. After playing with that cast for multiple weeks, Willis underwent a second surgery ahead of Week 17 due to complications, which caused him to miss his first-ever NFL game. That snapped a 63-game streak to start his career. Willis also played with a cast on his hand for parts of his junior season at Ole Miss and in 2010 with the 49ers.
Height said he took inspiration from Willis' mentality.
"I just thought of it as: ‘Something's just there,'" Height said. "It didn't stop my effort. It didn't stop me wanting to hunt the quarterback."

On the first play of the Broncos game, Height, seemingly out of the play after Jaylen Waddle had been tackled just beyond the line of scrimmage, sprinted over to the receiver and did a Superman leap over his body. Was it to test out his new piece of equipment? To see if he could still brace his fall with essentially one working hand?
"That was just me blacked out," Height said, "trying to get to the ball."

Height doesn't know how long he'll need to wear the cast during games. He doesn't care either, saying: "I mean, it's not really a difference for me. At the end of the day, I gotta go out and do my job."
"I love the way he competes, the way he plays," defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said. "He's gonna go out there regardless. He might have two clubs on and go out there. He's that kind of guy."

Thursday's practice: Nickel back Upton Stout (shoulder) returned to practice, wearing a blue non-contact jersey, after not participating on Wednesday. Head coach Kyle Shanahan had previously said the 49ers are hopeful Stout can play against Seattle.

Wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs) went from a limited participant Wednesday to a non-participant Thursday. Evans worked on a side field during the open viewing portion, as did defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) for the first time since suffering his injury ahead of a Week 3 practice. Shanahan said Thursday on KNBR that Bosa is "getting better each week," and that he is not "far from playing."
"We would love to get him out there before our bye week," Shanahan said of Bosa, "but still too early to tell."

Players who were upgraded to full participation on Thursday: running back Kaelon Black (illness), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (rest), running back Christian McCaffrey (rest) and tackle Trent Williams (rest).

articles.headline: Talarico’s influencer army privately frets about his 12-day absence from campaign trail, leaked Slack messages show
keyFacts: Leaked Slack messages reveal digital surrogates for Texas Senate candidate James Talarico privately expressed concern over his 12-day campaign absence.
Critics such as Donald Trump questioned Talarico's flu diagnosis, while poll aggregates show Talarico leading opponent Ken Paxton by 2.8 points.
Talarico's campaign spokesperson stated that Talarico will return to the campaign trail this weekend and attend an October 14 CNN town hall.
body: WASHINGTON — Texas Senate hopeful James Talarico’s social media influencer army has been privately fretting over his prolonged absence from the campaign trail, leaked Slack messages obtained by The Post reveal.
Privately on Wednesday, in a Slack channel featuring Talarico’s digital surrogates, several influencers raised tepid concerns about the messaging strategy amid his absence.
“I think it’ll be fine. It’s [j]ust conservatives blasting him. I’m just worried about him losing momentum,” Alex Balderas wrote in a group chat with influencers, featuring nearly 4,000 people.
“But I 100% expect him to make a comeback at the CNN [t]own hall that’s a given.”
Talarico is set to partake in a CNN town hall on Oct. 14. His campaign told The Post that Talarico will reemerge this weekend.
Critics, particularly allies of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, have raised doubts about whether influenza alone could explain why Talarico has been absent from the campaign trail for so long.
“TalaFREAKo has been missing for 12 days!” President Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday, deploying his preferred nickname for the lefty pol.

“Now, after looking for him throughout all of Texas, and beyond, probably even weirder places than anyone would think possible, he put out a statement that he has the ‘flu,’” the president continued. “12 days is a long time to rid yourself of the so-called flu bug.
“What’s going on?”
Talarico’s allies also suggested his campaign needs to provide more updates on his health.

“I suppose spokesman JT Ennis should come out and update on James health,” Balderas wrote in a Slack message Wednesday. “Conservatives doubting he’s sick but conservatives leaving out the important part.”
“James is diabetic that’s why it’s taking awhile for recovery so basically conservatives and Paxton are being. very immoral [sic].”
Elsewhere, in the leaked Slack chat, a campaign volunteer, Jacob Weber, shrugged off the consternation over Talarico’s whereabouts as a nothing burger.
“It’s a buncha people that don’t actually want him to be out touring that are causing a stink. Noone’s genuinely upset,” Weber wrote.
Balderas concurred in response, “Yeah it’s the conservatives they’re making it a big deal over two canceled events because he’s sick. But he’ll be back.”
“Hope James blast[s] Paxton for being absent the whole time after he won his runoff.”

Despite Texas being a red state, Talarico has run a remarkably competitive race against Paxton, notching a 2.8 percentage point edge over him, according to the latest RealClearPolitics aggregate of polls.
Paxton taunted Talarico with a proof-of-life demand on X. Trump also lashed out at Talarico.

“I hear the guy’s disappeared. Nobody knows,” Trump chided at a Wednesday rally. “You know where he is? He’s sick because he’s been forced to eat meat for political reasons, and he’s throwing up all over the place. He’s sick.”
“No, we’re all looking. Nobody can find the guy. He’s gone for two weeks, you know.”

On Truth Social, Trump further called for Talarico to debate Paxton, something his campaign quickly embraced, as it had been mounting a pressure campaign against the Texas attorney general to face him in a verbal bout for weeks.
When asked for comment about both the leaked Slack messages, Talarico’s campaign revealed that the state rep will return to the campaign trail soon.

“After holding more than 100 public events and shaking tens of thousands of hands, James came down with the flu but will be back on the trail this weekend,” Talarico spokesperson JT Ennis told The Post.

“Ken Paxton has been ignoring Texans this entire campaign, and his priorities are clear: he doesn’t answer to the people of this state — he answers to his billionaire megadonors and special interests.”
Over the past week and a half, Paxton has dealt with multiple stories based on a secret recording of his private remarks during a DC fundraiser last month.

In those recordings, Paxton ripped into the Iran war, grumbled over his lack of control over ad strategy amid a torrent of outside spending, and suggested Republicans’ numbers went down after the GOP midterm convention last month.

articles.headline: Google's head of data center design has jumped ship to Anthropic — so will this lead to a huge boost in capacity?
keyFacts: Google's former global design and construction chief, John M. Wilson, has joined Anthropic to oversee EMEA capacity delivery.
Anthropic has recruited multiple senior infrastructure and data center specialists from Google to build its computing capacity.
This migration of specialists raises a retention problem for Google that may require stronger incentives, according to the article.
body: - Anthropic is assembling a deep bench of former Google infrastructure specialists
- Google continues to lose veterans across critical data center functions to Anthropic
- John M. Wilson’s move adds another senior name to Anthropic’s infrastructure operation
Google’s former global design and construction chief John M. Wilson has joined Anthropic as a technical staff member overseeing EMEA capacity delivery.
Wilson spent six years at Google, where his responsibilities covered data center development and subsea infrastructure programs.
His arrival adds another senior infrastructure executive from Google to Anthropic, which has recruited several former employees for specialized data center roles.
A growing stream of Google infrastructure specialists
Anthropic has also recruited Winnie Leung, who now leads data center infrastructure, while Brett Rogers moved after overseeing construction activities at Google.
Liwen Mao, previously a staff data center system architect at Google, now leads Anthropic’s data center design activities.
Adam Johnson spent a decade at Google before joining Anthropic in October as its data center electrical lead, adding another experienced infrastructure specialist.
Peter Sarossy, a Google veteran of 20 years, joined Anthropic in January as a staff member working on data center security engineering.

Zach Miller also moved after 17 years at Google, taking responsibility for data center operations management within Anthropic’s infrastructure organization.
Scarlett Chen, previously involved with advanced technology and innovation at Google, now works at Anthropic as a member of technical staff.
The hiring pattern extends beyond engineering, with Sana Ouji joining Anthropic’s energy team in April to help expand its data center portfolio.
Mike Brinker followed from Google a month later, taking responsibility for capacity delivery, while Asad Malik subsequently joined to lead compute finance strategy.
The series of appointments gives Anthropic personnel with experience spanning construction, electrical systems, security, operations, energy, capacity planning and infrastructure finance.
That range covers several functions required when a technology company needs to develop and operate increasingly large computing facilities.
Wilson brings major infrastructure experience to Anthropic
Before Google, Wilson served as Amazon’s European design and construction leader, giving him experience across major technology infrastructure projects.
His earlier career also included roles as chief of staff in the British Army and infrastructure director at NATO.
Wilson described his move as another demanding infrastructure assignment, citing the scale and importance of his responsibilities at Anthropic.
"Leading global infrastructure delivery across data centers and subsea programs taught me two enduring truths," Wilson said on LinkedIn.
"Scale is humbling, but high-trust teams make the extraordinary feel routine. Clear intent, rigorous operational control, and calm execution will always beat complexity."
Speaking on his new role, Wilson said: “The stakes and scale have never been higher, and I’m eager to get stuck in.”
His new assignment specifically covers EMEA capacity delivery, giving him responsibility for infrastructure expansion across Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
Anthropic’s recruitment of multiple Google infrastructure specialists comes as the company continues to build its personnel around data center capacity.

For Google, the steady migration of senior infrastructure specialists raises a retention problem that may require stronger incentives, clearer career paths and measures to keep critical expertise from walking out the door.

articles.headline: Will Ethiopia’s neighbours intervene as Tigray war escalates?
keyFacts: Ethiopian federal forces entered Tigray's capital of Mekelle as rebel alliance forces withdrew from the city.
Tigrayan rebel leaders pledged to continue fighting, while reports emerged of Eritrean troops entering northern Tigray towns.
Analysts stated that a prolonged conflict across multiple fronts could potentially involve regional rivals like Egypt and Eritrea.
body: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia – After nearly two weeks of fierce fighting, Ethiopian federal forces entered the Tigrayan capital of Mekelle as forces from an alliance of rebel groups, including the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), withdrew from the city.
The fighting that erupted late last month has effectively ended the 2022 Pretoria ceasefire and the fragile peace that followed the devastating Tigray war.

But Mekelle’s capture may mark the end of conventional warfare rather than the end of the conflict. Fighting has continued elsewhere in Tigray, while reports of Eritrean troops entering northern Tigrayan towns have added a potentially more dangerous regional dimension.

Ethiopian federal forces used air power and ground forces to advance across Tigray. After suffering successive defeats around the towns of Alamata and Kobo, rebel forces withdrew into the surrounding countryside. They have pledged to continue fighting.
“We will confront the enemy on our terms and where we choose,” TPLF leader Debretsion Gebremichael said.
A war that may not be over

There are echoes of the war that began in 2020, when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government declared victory after federal forces captured Mekelle. Tigrayan forces subsequently regrouped in the mountains, retook much of the region and recaptured the capital, prolonging the war for nearly a year and a half.

The renewed conflict could follow a similar trajectory, particularly if the TPLF and other armed groups succeed in turning the mountainous terrain into a prolonged armed rebellion. Ethiopia is already fighting insurgencies in Amhara and Oromia, raising the prospect of its federal forces being stretched across multiple fronts.

But the battlefield reversals suffered by the rebels could have implications well beyond Tigray. They have raised concern in Egypt and among other Ethiopian rivals, according to Hossamaldeen Ibrahim, an African analyst at the Bloomsbury Intelligence and Security Institute.

“Egypt views the Renaissance Dam, and any Ethiopian [army] move towards the Red Sea, as a strategic threat, so it has allied with Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia against any Ethiopian unilateralism,” Ibrahim told Al Jazeera.
“Ethiopia is seeking a sea outlet; Eritrea sees this as an existential threat.”
Ethiopia’s Red Sea ambitions
Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea won its war of independence in 1991, leaving Addis Ababa heavily dependent on neighbouring countries for access to international trade.
Abiy has increasingly made access to the Red Sea a strategic priority since 2023, raising concerns in Eritrea over Ethiopia’s ambitions, particularly over the port of Assab.
Ethiopia currently relies heavily on Djibouti for maritime trade, while also pursuing alternative arrangements, including through Kenya and Somaliland.
After being sworn in on Monday for another five-year term following his party’s victory in the June 1 election, Abiy again put the issue at the centre of his parliamentary address.
“Based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea,” he told parliament.
The issue has increasingly become part of a wider regional contest.
A loose regional alignment

In recent months, Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia have found themselves sharing concerns over Ethiopia’s regional ambitions. On October 4, the leaders of the four countries met for a quadrilateral consultative summit in New Alamein, Egypt, where they discussed regional issues and pledged to strengthen political, economic and trade cooperation as well as consultation and coordination.

The meeting does not amount to a formal military alliance, and the four countries have different interests in their dealings with Addis Ababa. The summit’s joint declaration also called for respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, noninterference in internal affairs and the peaceful resolution of disputes.
But their concerns increasingly overlap around Ethiopia’s ambitions in the Red Sea, the Nile and the wider Horn of Africa.

Relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea have also deteriorated sharply since the Pretoria ceasefire. Ethiopia closed its embassy in Eritrea and expelled Eritrean diplomats on October 1, accusing Asmara of hostile acts and involvement in the renewed fighting. Eritrea responded by severing diplomatic ties, while denying that it supported the opposition alliance. Egypt and Sudan have also denied Ethiopian accusations that they are backing the alliance.
The Ethiopian army’s advance into Tigray has added another layer to that rivalry.

“The [Ethiopian army’s] advance in Tigray directly threatens [Eritrean President] Isaias [Afwerki] and the Eritrean state,” said Etana H Dinka, an assistant professor of African history at the University of Miami.

Eritrean forces fought alongside Ethiopian troops during the 2020–22 Tigray war, but relations between Abiy and Isaias have since deteriorated. Eritrean troops have reportedly been seen in towns in northern Tigray, adding a potentially significant new dimension to the conflict. The Associated Press news agency reported Eritrean troops entering Adigrat and Idaga Hamus after crossing into Ethiopia, while Eritrea has neither confirmed nor denied the troop movements.
Eritrea’s role could be decisive
For Eritrea, the location of the fighting matters as much as its outcome.

A prolonged conflict in Tigray could keep Ethiopian forces tied down and limit Addis Ababa’s ability to pursue its Red Sea ambitions. But a decisive Ethiopian victory could leave the federal government with greater freedom to turn its attention towards regional rivals.

“With reports that Eritrean troops are moving into Tigray, Eritrea seems keen on boosting TPLF forces withdrawing northwards, so that the engagement between Ethiopian and Eritrean soldiers takes place in Tigrayan territory, and not in Eritrea,” said Mohamed Kheir Omer, a researcher focused on the Horn of Africa.
That could create an incentive for Eritrea to support forces capable of keeping the Ethiopian army tied down, without necessarily entering a direct confrontation of its own.
Sudan adds another layer
Sudan’s war adds another dimension to the regional rivalry.

Egypt has provided political backing and logistical and technical support to Sudan’s army, according to the Reuters news agency, while the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have been accused of atrocities in Darfur.

Ethiopia has faced accusations of facilitating support for the RSF. A Reuters investigation reported in February that Ethiopia was hosting a camp in its western Benishangul-Gumuz region where thousands of fighters linked to the RSF were being trained. Reuters cited eight sources, including a senior Ethiopian government official, who said the United Arab Emirates financed the camp’s construction and provided military trainers and logistical support. The UAE denied the allegations, and Reuters said it could not independently verify the UAE’s role.
Those competing relationships are part of a broader contest over the Nile, Sudan, the Red Sea and access to trade routes.

For Egypt, its dispute with Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam remains a major strategic concern. For Eritrea, Ethiopia’s search for a Red Sea outlet is viewed through the lens of national security. For Sudan’s neighbours, the conflict threatens to reshape regional power balances.
Will Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia intervene?
The shared interests of Ethiopia’s regional rivals do not necessarily translate into direct intervention.

Egypt has its own calculations over the Nile and Sudan. Eritrea has a direct security interest in developments in Tigray. Somalia is dealing with its own security challenges and a complicated relationship with Addis Ababa. Sudan remains consumed by its devastating civil war.
At the same time, Ethiopia’s federal forces now face the possibility of fighting on several fronts.

The TPLF, Amhara Fano and the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA) have each sought to challenge the federal government in different parts of the country. If they can maintain pressure on the army while retreating from major population centres, the fall of Mekelle could prove to be only the first phase of a much longer conflict.
For Ethiopia’s rivals, the question is whether to exploit that vulnerability or avoid being drawn into another regional war.
The extent of any regional involvement may ultimately depend on whether the TPLF can keep federal forces tied down in Tigray, and away from the Eritrean border.

“It isn’t difficult to understand Cairo’s commitment to prevent Ethiopia from succeeding in the current warfare, whatever its army’s intended goals, including Abiy’s acclaimed access to the Red Sea, are,” University of Miami’s Dinka said.
The question now is whether those regional calculations will remain largely diplomatic or spill into the battlefield.

articles.headline: The long-deployed USS Lincoln returns home to San Diego Bay
keyFacts: The USS Lincoln returned to San Diego after a 10-month deployment supporting combat operations against Iran.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded the crew the Presidential Unit Citation for executing nearly 3,700 combat missions.
The USS George Washington relieved the Lincoln in the Middle East in August.
body: The long-deployed USS Lincoln returns home to San Diego Bay

CORONADO, Calif. — After more than 10 months at sea, thousands of sailors Thursday poured out of the the USS Lincoln on San Diego Bay to thunderous cheers, streaming tears and emotional hugs, marking a homecoming that included new dads who met babies born while they were away on a historic deployment supporting the Iran war.

The reunion followed an emotional rollercoaster for families who described crying and losing sleep after hearing reports of supply shortages and deteriorating mental health among the crew during the deployment that spent a record 265 days of uninterrupted time at sea. Many said they only could communicate with family via the occasional email or rare WhatsApp calls.
Abel Ramirez, 20, was glad to have that all behind him. He walked off the carrier with a big grin, overjoyed that his first deployment was over.
"It feels amazing," he said while headed out to search for his parents who traveled from Texas. "There was a certain point when I never thought I would come off."
Cassity Garduque, 14, waved as her mom in her sailor uniform frantically waved back from the top deck after the ship docked at the pier.
"It feels really overwhelming," she said about being seeing her mom again. "She missed most of my seventh grade and my birthday."
She added that she's happy her mom won't be eating ramen almost every day and can celebrate with her now.

Capt. Daniel Keeler, the ship's commander, said most of the crew was on their first deployment and that the issues they faced were normal for such a long deployment, adding everyone had access to four meals a day.
"It's a floating city as you can see and at any moment there might be a clogged toilet," he said.
The Navy has downplayed problems on the carrier
The Navy initially downplayed any problems during the deployment, and President Donald Trump commented in August that the Lincoln's lengthy deployment was "not nearly long enough."
Navy leaders eventually acknowledged there were some issues aboard.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew out to the Lincoln on Wednesday to give the crew the Presidential Unit Citation, the highest honor a unit can receive.

Hegseth told the crew that "what makes the U.S. military and the U.S. Navy and all these sailors different is that you adapt and that you're resilient and you overcome — you finish the mission nonetheless."
Hegseth pushed back against what he said were efforts to turn the "Lincoln into some sort of a symbol, a symbol of dysfunction or a symbol of low morale or a symbol of a failed mission."
USS Lincoln crew looks forward to family and favorite meals

The Lincoln, which set a record for uninterrupted time at sea, is the second carrier to endure an unusually long deployment during the Iran war and to receive the Presidential Unit Citation afterward, typically reserved for significant achievement in combat.

The crew of the USS Gerald R. Ford returned in May from a 326-day deployment — the longest for an aircraft carrier in the past 50 years and a record in the post-Vietnam War era. The Lincoln's deployment of 322 days was just shy of that.

Among the first to depart the carrier at the naval base in Coronado were 64 fathers meeting their babies for the first time, the Navy said. With the airwing included, there were 122 new dads, Keeler said.
Waiting for the Lincoln to bring her husband home, sailor Kathy Monterrosa held her 6-month-old daughter, Sarahi, outfitted in a tiny blue and white sailor dress.
"She's our deployment baby," said Monterrosa, of Virginia Beach, Virginia.
It was tough to hear about the ship's conditions while she was pregnant, she said. "I was crying a lot and worried. I wasn't sure if he was OK or not," she said.
When she finally heard from her husband, he told her it was "pretty bad," but now she said she feels blessed to have her family home.
Sailor Steven Rivas beamed as he held is 7-month-old daughter.

"I couldn't grasp the reality of it," he said about coming home. He became overwhelmed as they pulled into the bay, "seeing everyone and knowing my family was waiting for me," Rivas said, his voice shaking as his eyes teared up.
Alma Solano Velez said her husband gave his family an extensive list of the foods he has been craving over the past 10 months: oxtail, barbecue chicken, broccoli and shrimp empanadas to name a few.
He had told his wife about "the lack of food and showers" on board and was looking forward to seeing their daughter, who turned 4 while he was away, she said.
The carrier left San Diego in November and arrived in the Middle East in January. U.S. and Israeli forces launched airstrikes against Iran on Feb. 28.
In August, acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the Lincoln maintained adequate food supplies, but because combat operations limited resupply opportunities, meal options were reduced for a short time.
After more than 10 months at sea, the Lincoln's crew got a stop in Thailand early last month on the way back from the Middle East.
Long deployments can tax service members
Extended naval deployments can wear on service members who are away from home for long periods and increase strain on the ship and its equipment.
The Navy told lawmakers that eight sailors attempted suicide during the record-setting deployment, though experts say that number is low in a strike group of 6,000 sailors over 10 months.

According to the citation that Hegseth read to the crew, the Lincoln and its strike group executed nearly 3,700 combat missions, launched 450 Tomahawk cruise missiles, shot down 77 one-way attack drones, sank 64 Iranian warships, and destroyed 21 anti-ship cruise missiles.
Another carrier, the usually Asia-based USS George Washington, relieved the Lincoln in the Middle East in August.

articles.headline: After 4 Hours, Phantom Blade Zero Just Became My Most-Anticipated Action Game
keyFacts: Polygon played four hours of the action game Phantom Blade Zero, developed by S-Game, focusing on its combat and boss battles.
Director Soulframe Liang stated the game follows an assassin named Soul who has 66 days to live after receiving a new heart.
Phantom Blade Zero is scheduled for release on October 29 for PlayStation 5 and Windows PC.
body: Action game fans have had no shortage of choice in 2026. Romeo Is a Dead Man spotlights blood-soaked hack-and-slash combat, Beast of Reincarnation offers Souls-adjacent parry-focused fighting, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword takes parrying to the extreme with a plethora of defensive options.

Phantom Blade Zero looks to carve out its own space among sword-slashing action games. It blends simple controls and intense parries with stylish wuxia animations to create one of the most anticipated non-GTA 6 games of the fall release calendar. I recently got to play around four hours of Phantom Blade Zero on Windows PC at a preview event hosted by developer S-Game in Beijing, China, and experienced the game’s unique take on melee action.

I played from the very beginning of the game until the end of its first chapter. Afterward, I was plopped into two separate boss fights, defeating one and losing against the other. Trading blows with Phantom Blade Zero’s bosses was certainly the highlight of my time with S-Game’s ambitious martial arts game, though the moment-to-moment action in between those boss fights didn’t reach the same highs.
John Wick meets Wuxia

I played as Soul, an assassin being hounded by members of The Order, a shadowy organization he used to work for. Maybe it was the jet lag after a 16.5-hour flight, but I didn’t pick up on that context in the preview; I learned Soul was a John Wick-style assassin on the run when director Soulframe Liang mentioned it during a roundtable interview following the gameplay session.

Soul gets mortally wounded fighting his childhood BFF Zuo Shang, and both dudes stab each other through the heart. Don’t worry, Soul doesn't die (yet) — a creepy little guy called the Flesh Sculptor hooks him up with a new heart, but it’ll only last 66 days. Zuo Shang also survives, and now Souls sets off on an action-packed adventure to presumably find and battle his old friend once and for all.

Nothing about the story really grabbed me in these opening hours, but, to be frank, the stories of action games like Black Myth: Wukong, Stellar Blade, and Beast of Reincarnation didn’t grab me much either, and I still put dozens of hours into those games. The real crux of Phantom Blade Zero’s appeal is its combat, which, after the preview session, I look forward to experiencing in full.
‘A playable kung fu movie’

S-Game’s stated goal is to bring Chinese martial arts to life through Phantom Blade Zero’s combat. Soulframe wanted to translate the cinema of wuxia films to action-packed gameplay and to “create a playable kung fu movie.” S-Game has recruited movie star and martial artist Donnie Yen to help bring its vision to life as a creative consultant, and he’s even playing and mo-caping a character in the game.

Yen leads a team of about 15-20 stunt performers and helps choreograph the action, which is full of the stuntmen performing lightning-fast choreography that sometimes involves wirework stunts, like in wuxia movies. Kenji Tanigaki — best known for directing The Furious, widely considered the best action movie of the year — is a part of Yen’s team as an action director.

With Yen, Tanigaki, and more martial arts masters on board, S-Game succeeds in its goal, as every animation has an over-the-top flourish. Soul won’t just advance on an enemy and strike, but whirl his sword around, air trials following it, with a certain panache as he attacks. He won’t just climb up a ledge, but dramatically leap upward and do a little spinny spin to land. Everything about Phantom Blade Zero’s style is so extra, which lends the game a certain charm, even when frightening monster enemies are barreling down upon you.

While Phantom Blade Zero nails the look of kung fu, at the end of the day I’m still just mashing Square and Triangle, cool animation or not. The more I play, the more I discover the combat’s depth, however. Key to that depth is Soul’s Sha-chi meter, which is like a stamina meter for his most powerful combos.

In an early boss fight, I learn just how crucial Sha-chi is to the combat. Switching weapons refills the meter, meaning I can exhaust Soul’s Sha-chi with devastating attacks, switch to my other equipped weapon, and keep the party going with a refilled Sha-chi meter. It’s a lot like discovering how transforming your trick weapon mid-combo in Bloodborne can unleash a heavy blow.

Boss battles are certainly the highlight of Phantom Blade Zero. Though the cadence of them isn’t as quick as in a game like Black Myth Wukong (which feels more like a boss rush game at times), they still come fast and furious. The combat really shines in tough boss battles, whereas encounters with regular enemies can feel too paint-by-numbers and end too quickly. I lost count of just how many bosses I tackled in the preview, from an enemy on a horse-drawn carriage to a foe who conjures additional arms mid-battle, essentially becoming a sickle-wielding General Grievous.

The session concluded with two later-game boss battles, both of which were quite tough. The first was against a woman who flitted on the air and summoned what looked like paper mache dragons from the ground. (I was too busy trying not to die to admire their design.) She was a challenge, and had two phases. Thankfully, an ally joined in for the second phase, and I’m hopeful more boss fights in Phantom Blade Zero will have NPCs fighting alongside Soul. I always enjoy having a partner along for the ride.

I only got one attempt at the second boss fight due to time constraints on my play session, but it had some of the most notable sequences in Phantom Blade Zero I saw. I fought against two dancers controlling a lion head puppet; after the first was defeated, the second summoned little enemies, each with their own lion heads. I defeated them, and picked up one of their lion heads to shoot fire at the boss while dodging his blasts and fire by jumping from one raised pole to another. It was immensely exciting, and made me wonder what other creative fights are up S-Game’s sleeve. (You can watch a full fight against this boss at the end of August’s Phantom Blade Zero State of Play.)
Everything else you need to know about Phantom Blade Zero

Now that the September flood of new releases has passed, Phantom Blade Zero might be the biggest upcoming game for the rest of 2026 that’s not about committing crime in Fake Florida. There’s a lot to unpack from the game still, so let’s break down what’s left to learn about S-Game’s playable martial arts movie.
- Phantom Blade Zero will be about 35-40 hours long for players who are experienced with action games. Soulframe said the density of the experience is more important than its breadth.
- More than 30 weapons will be available with 20 more Phantom Edges, which are more akin to special attacks than usable weapons.
- Phantom Blade Zero is a largely linear game, but there are some light Metroidvania elements. Some Phantom Edges will be used in traversal and allow Soul to explore previously inaccessible areas.
- Difficulty options! Phantom Blade Zero will feature three difficulty options to start — your expected easy, medium, and hard. They can be changed at any time. However…

- If you lower the difficulty to easy mode, you can’t go back up. I found this out the hard way during a boss fight I just wanted to clear so I could continue the demo, and had to play the rest of the way on Phantom Blade Zero’s lowest difficulty.
- An additional 66 Days difficulty can be unlocked. Each time Soul dies, you lose a day until there are none left.

- It’s not clear how much Soul’s in-game 66 days will matter. After one cutscene, the days count reduced by one, but I’m not sure what significance this has outside of Soul getting one step closer to death. On regular difficulties, I don’t expect Soul’s 66 days to manifest as a fundamental mechanic (like in The Blood of Dawnwalker), though it does appear to serve a narrative purpose of some sort.

- Boss fights are tough, but, unlike in a FromSoftware Soulslike, there are checkpoints between phases. If you defeat a boss’ first phase but falter in the second, you can tackle the fight from the midway point on your next attempt.
Phantom Blade Zero will be released Oct. 29 for PlayStation 5 and Windows PC.

articles.headline: Chief Justice John Roberts gives FCC temporary win in fight over favorable campaign ad rate rules
keyFacts: Chief Justice John Roberts temporarily halted a lower court order requiring the FCC to quickly rule on favorable political advertising rates.
Democrats challenged the FCC ad rate rule due to candidate cash advantages, while Republicans supported it due to party-level fundraising strengths.
Roberts ordered Democratic candidates to respond to emergency petitions by Saturday while the Supreme Court weighs the cases.
body: Chief Justice John Roberts gave the Federal Communications Commission a temporary win on Thursday in its legal battle over who is entitled to favorable advertising rates in the closing weeks of the costly and hotly contested midterm elections.

Roberts granted an administrative stay of a ruling by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit that would have forced the FCC to issue a final ruling on a revised rule allowing political parties and joint fundraising committees to access the more favorable television advertisement rates that are typically reserved for political candidates. The Democratic congressional candidates who brought the challenge are hoping to strike down the revised rule due to their cash advantage with individual candidates, and Republicans have pushed for the new rule due to their significant cash advantage at the party level.

Last month, the Supreme Court ruled 8-1 that the 4th Circuit had prematurely halted the rule, finding that the FCC must issue a decision on the Democratic candidates’ petition for review before the appeals court can get involved. On Wednesday, a three-judge panel on the 4th Circuit ordered the FCC to issue its decision by Friday, a move the Trump administration claims is to allow the appeals court to strike down the rule with less than a month to go before the elections.

Roberts halted the 4th Circuit’s ruling for now, pausing that deadline while the Supreme Court weighs the emergency petitions from both the Trump administration and the GOP Senate and House campaign arms to lift the lower court’s ruling.
The chief justice ordered the Democratic candidates to respond to the emergency petitions by 5 p.m. on Saturday but did not set a firm timeline for when the high court will rule on the petitions.
DOJ PULLS SUPREME COURT INTO FCC FIGHT OVER FAVORABLE CAMPAIGN AD RATES
The fight over the FCC rule comes with less than a month to go in the fiercely contested and expensive midterm elections, with control of both the House and Senate at stake.

The Thursday applications are the latest election-related case to make its way to the Supreme Court’s emergency docket in recent months. The other major fight on the emergency docket over the past several months has been regarding the Trump administration’s new mail ballot order, which the high court allowed to remain blocked through the midterm elections.

articles.headline: USS Abraham Lincoln’s commanding officer addresses suicide attempts in strike group after record deployment – live
keyFacts: Captain Dan Keeler said there were no suicides on the USS Abraham Lincoln, addressing reports of strike group suicide attempts.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth falsely claimed that former President Barack Obama called the 2009 Fort Hood shooting workplace violence.
Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers debated over tariffs and rhetoric in their first televised matchup.
body: USS Abraham Lincoln’s commanding officer addresses suicide attempts in strike group

In a brief news conference on Thursday afternoon, Captain Dan Keeler, the USS Abraham Lincoln’s commanding officer, addressed widespread reports of mental health challenges faced by his crew during their long deployment.

“For most of my sailors, that this was their first time away from home, their first deployment, their first experience with combat,” Keeler said. “I understand the anxiety that that might have caused, but I can tell you this: our team of professionals on the ship led every single one of those sailors through that experience, and the great majority responded like sailors always do - with honor, courage, and commitment.”

“They are fantastic, fantastic sailors and marines, and they’re going to be cared for continuously on the next coming few months,” he added. “I deployed with five chaplains and a very well staffed mental health team. We got our sailors any care they needed and got them back in the fight when it was appropriate.”
Near the end of the news conference one reporter asked: “Were there some sailors who did try to commit suicide or jump overboard?”
“The key number that I like to focus on is zero; there were no suicides on board. There were no lost lives on on board,” Keeler replied.

“The suicide attempt number,” he went on. “You know, the secretary of the navy put out a number that encompassed the entirety of the strike group,” Keeler said, referring to a letter to Congress from acting navy secretary Hung Cao last month in which he wrote that there had been a total of eight suicide attempts across all the ships in the strike group led by the Lincoln.

“I think that key point has been lost when he, the secretary of the navy, put out the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group, that encompasses several thousand more sailors than what’s on board behind me,” Keeler added.

“We want the suicide attempt number to be zero. Having done this many, many times with the demographics that I have on board and the, you know, the stressful mission that we conduct, that’s unrealistic,” he continued. “That’s why I go to sea with a very, very well staffed mental health team. And when we had acute mental health cases, they immediately get seen by that mental health team and evaluated.”
Hegseth joins Trump in trying to politicize the 2009 Fort Hood attack by falsely claiming Obama called rampage 'workplace violence'

In an interview on Thursday with the rightwing network Real America’s Voice, Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, joined Donald Trump in trying to use the 2009 shooting rampage at Fort Hood in Texas to attack former president Barack Obama.
On Wednesday night, Trump made the wildly false claim that Obama had emails from the attacker describing his plans in advance but chose not to stop him.

Speaking on Thursday to the far-right influencer Jack Posobiec, who helped spread the debunked Pizzagate conspiracy theory to smear Democrats in 2016, the defense secretary announced that Nidal Hasan, the former army psychiatrist who killed 12 soldiers and one civilian at Fort Hood, would be executed by firing squad later this year.
Hegseth, a former Fox News host, then falsely claimed that Obama had downplayed the attack.
“It was a radical Islamist terror attack,” Hegseth said. “Remember what Obama called it? ‘Workplace violence,’” the defense secretary said, falsely, as Posobiec nodded vigorously.

“I mean, that’s what we’re up against. That’s the worldview we’re up against, it’s ‘workplace violence,’” the supposedly nonpartisan defense secretary continued, referring, incorrectly, to a controversy over how the US military categorized the deaths of the 12 active-duty soldiers killed by Hasan at the time.

Relatives of those killed in the attack by a Muslim service member who later called it revenge for US military operations against Muslim countries, were enraged that the military refused to classify those killed as victims of combat or terrorism, since they were not deployed to Iraq or Afghanistan at the time.

The families sued in federal court, claiming that “the Army has refused to deem the soldiers killed and wounded in the attack eligible for a Purple Heart decoration, with its attendant recognition and medical and retirement benefits.” The suit, which criticized Obama for failing to call the attack terrorism, was dismissed in 2019.

While some experts, including the political philosopher Michael Walzer, have argued that the definition of terrorism should be reserved for attacks on civilians, and exclude soldiers, Republicans continued to criticize Obama for not describing the attack as an act of terrorism, even though he appeared to do so in a 2013 speech at the National Defense University.
After describing the threat from foreign groups that plot “acts of terror” in that address, Obama said, “we face a real threat from radicalized individuals here in the United States.”

“Deranged or alienated individuals - often US citizens or legal residents - can do enormous damage, particularly when inspired by larger notions of violent jihad,” Obama added. “And that pull towards extremism appears to have led to the shooting at Fort Hood and the bombing of the Boston Marathon.”

Mike Rogers has continually leaned into Islamophobic rhetoric against Abdul El-Sayed, attempting to tie him to Hamas and the Muslim Brotherhood. The two are repeatedly sparring, with the moderator struggling to keep them on track.
Rogers claimed El-Sayed has refused to condemn a terrorist attack in Michigan earlier this year or the 7 October Hamas terrorist attacks in Gaza, though El-Sayed noted he has condemned both.
But, El-Sayed added, “I’m not somebody who tries to make political theater out of other people’s pain.”
He also retorted to Rogers: “Did you sell your yachts?” Rogers responded: “I never owned a yacht in Florida, brother.”
After a 30-second commercial break, moderator Rick Albin said that in his 30 years of doing debates, he’d never seen the sparring continue during the commercial break, but tonight, it did.

The televised Michigan Senate debate, between Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan, and Mike Rogers, the Republican candidate, quickly moved on to the topic of tariffs, particularly those on imports from Canada, which affect Michigan as a US-Canada border state. Rogers this week backtracked on previous support for Trump’s tariffs on Canada, saying in a campaign ad that “Canada is not our enemy” and that the “tariff war” needed to end now.

During the debate, Rogers said he called the commerce secretary this week to advocate for a deal between the two countries. He said there are tariffs in place that are “too high and not helpful for us”.
“I’d like to see it end. I think we need to end it,” Rogers said.

El-Sayed said he supports targeted, logical tariffs that protect Michigan manufacturing, but nothing like the “ham-fisted, chaotic, self-serving” tariffs Trump put in place. He called out Rogers for “flip-flopping” on the issue, saying he only is reversing his stance because of “sagging poll numbers”.
“He’s doing an ad drinking a Labatt and talking about the Red Wings, pretending like he was not for this the entire time,” El-Sayed said. “Be serious, my guy. Like, just be serious.”
Dr Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, is now debating his Republican opponent, former congressman Mike Rogers, for the first time.
The debate is being streamed live by the NBC affiliate WOOD TV.
Several recent polls show El-Sayed, a former public health official, leading by a slim margin over Rogers.

The tight race has drawn national attention as Republicans fight to keep control of Congress. Questions have swirled over whether the progressive El-Sayed can prevail in a state that elected Donald Trump in 2024.

If El-Sayed were to win the contest, he would make history as the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. His opponents have targeted El-Sayed’s faith and sharp criticism of the Israeli military campaign in Gaza.
In a thinly veiled attack on his faith, Trump incorrectly referred to the Democrat as “Mohammed El-Sayed” and a “Terrorist Sympathizer,” in a social media tirade on Wednesday.

“He knows my name is Abdul,” El-Sayed replied. “He thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor’s office.”

body: Patrick Mahomes is back with the Kansas City Chiefs, and this team is 4-0 to start its season. So, all is well in Chiefs Kingdom, because winning is exactly what this franchise is used to doing.

One of the biggest question marks heading into the 2026-27 season was if and when Mahomes would be fully recovered from his ACL and LCL tear. Well, the good news is that he's back and looking stronger than ever. He's even doing one thing better than he did before the injury.

Bill Barnwell of ESPN has released his official NFL quarter-season awards after Week 4. Here, he praises Mahomes for his work this year and even names him Comeback Player of the Year. That really shouldn't be surprising, of course.
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is more accurate on deep passes
In the feature, Barnwell says Mahomes has "returned from a torn ACL and looked, frankly, better than the guy we saw over the past few years."
He adds, "The addition of Kenneth Walker III has gone a long way, but Mahomes has been more accurate as a deep passer while retaining his ability to throw off platform like nobody else in football."
So, the thing Mahomes has been doing better is that he's more accurate on deep passes and still makes the off-platform throws that make him so great on the field.

During the 2026 season so far, Mahomes has recorded 1,037 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns and just two interceptions through four games. His 4-0 record also says a lot, as the player is responsible for getting points on the board. If Mahomes keeps this up, there's no reason this team can't go deep, as usual.

articles.headline: Apple reportedly plans touchscreen MacBook and iPad Mini launch for this month
keyFacts: According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple is expected to debut its first touchscreen laptop on or around October 27.
The rumored touchscreen MacBook will reportedly run on M5 Pro and Max chips and feature an interface that adapts to different inputs.
Anonymous sources said Apple also plans to present a redesigned iPad Mini and introduce new smart home gadgets on October 13.
body: Apple reportedly plans touchscreen MacBook and iPad Mini launch for this month
The wait to (literally) get your hands on the tech may almost be over.

2026 is turning into a big year for Apple hardware news. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the company's first touchscreen laptop is expected to debut "on or around" October 27. So, not a 100-percent solid date for a product announcement, but still a more concrete time frame than we've ever had about Apple's long-awaited touchscreen laptop debut.

Rumors about a touchscreen edition of Apple's high-end laptop date back to 2023. The more recent chatter about this device, largely driven by Gurman's reports, is that it will have a dynamic interface that adapts to the different modes of input. We're expecting the new touchscreen MacBook, potentially called MacBook Ultra, to run on the same M5 Pro and Max chips as the current high-end MacBook Pro models, as an earlier report suggested there won't be pro-level versions of the new M6 chip.

In addition to touchscreen laptops, the anonymous Bloomberg sources said to expect Apple's presentation to include a redesigned iPad Mini with an OLED display, and smaller updates to the entry level 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac to add the new M6 chip that debuted with the Mac mini refresh. The entry-level MacBook Pro currently runs an M5 chip, while the iMac is stuck on an M4 chip. And that won't be Apple's only set of reveals this month; it's also slated to introduce a new collection of smart home gadgets on October 13. This packed event schedule follows the summertime debut of Apple's first foldable in the iPhone Duo.

articles.headline: Why are more roofs not made of solar tiles?
keyFacts: Tesla stopped offering solar roofs following disappointing sales, which significantly impacted the solar roof industry.
Solar roofs can cost twice as much as standard solar panels and are less efficient at producing energy.
Some companies are adopting matrix shingling technology and automated design software to lower costs and improve solar roof efficiency.
body: - Published
Some people in the US "still hate the look of solar", Kate Collardson acknowledges.

She would know. Collardson handles operations for the Solar Service of Colorado, a solar maintenance and inspection company. She's also held just about every other job in the industry, from installer to instructor.
For those that hate the look of solar panels, an alternative is a solar roof, where the tiles (or shingles) house solar cells, but look much the same as regular tiles.
This is especially important for historic buildings, where heritage rules limit changes to their appearance.

For many people, the first time they'd heard of this product category was in August, when Tesla's website stopped offering solar roofs, external. This followed disappointing sales and a lawsuit over sudden price hikes, external.
Other companies have also pulled out, but Tesla's decision in particular sent shockwaves through the solar roof industry.
Some see it as a death knell for solar tiles; others, as an opportunity.
For instance, the small Swiss company Freesuns is considering expanding to the US.
Deborah Learoyd, Freesuns' CEO and managing director, estimates that the company's sales have grown 20â30% since it was established in 2019.
In general, solar roof components continue to be manufactured in smaller batches. This limits the economies of scale and standardisation, though flexible manufacturing could help somewhat.

Learoyd says that while the unit costs for Freesuns' products are slowly decreasing, "a lot of the cost is actually the fact that every roof is a little bit different. And so it has to be engineered a little bit differently, installed a little bit differently".
Solar roofs typically require collaboration among roofers, solar installers and electricians. And building regulations tend to be more complex than for solar panels.

The additional time and paperwork can take a toll on a roofing business, Collardson explains. "You try to put a roofer into the equation and they're going, 'This is taking forever. I'm losing money. I could have sold 10 roofing jobs in the time that it takes me to sell this one'."
Collardson has to charge more for repair of solar shingles, compared to a standard photovoltaic (PV) setup.

She explains, "With traditional solar, we generally have electronics on the panel and a map that shows us exactly how much each panel is producing." So when something goes wrong, it's easy to spot where.
"With solar shingles, we don't really have the benefit of that mapping; there's no room underneath the shingle for the electronics." Thermal cameras can identify the trouble spots, however.

But then there's the matter of accessing them. "You can remove the one in the middle of the array, but you have to walk on the others, and you really shouldn't walk on them because you're going to create micro-fractures and that's going to cause issues down the road."
Before repair costs are factored in, a solar roof might cost twice as much as a system of solar panels mounted on a roof.
Solar roofs are also less efficient - one reason is that the tiles are just smaller.
Another factor is the energy lost as heat. Since the tiles sit close to the roof, there's less airflow than with standard solar panels mounted on a roof. Heat impairs solar performance.

Coloured tiles are even less efficient, comments Ben Graves, co-founder of UK solar company Sunsave. "The reason why all solar cells are black, and increasingly the whole panel is now black, is because black is the best absorbing colour."
Overall, much more space would need to be devoted to solar roof tiles to produce the same amount of energy.
Sunsave does not offer solar roofs. "Most people in the UK just don't have enough money to pay for it," Graves believes.
While appearance was a bigger factor five years ago, now "the vast majority of consumers are most interested in how much they can save".
But supporters of solar roofs argue that they should not be pitted against standard solar modules on roofs.

"Let's not compare PV roof tiles to a standard PV system, but look at PV roof tiles as generating additional electricity from our roofs instead of just having the roof sit there," urges Martin Heinrich who leads a research group at the Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems in Germany.
While standard solar panels have gone from strength to strength, solar roofs have not advanced to the same extent.
One advancement that could especially help solar roofs is matrix shingling technology.

This is a different way of connecting solar cells. The solar cells are cut into narrow strips, layered like overlapping shingles, and connected to each other using electrically conductive adhesive, rather than metal wires.

This means that the electrical current can flow around shaded areas, unlike with standard modules. "If you get like a bird pooping on a part of the cell, the current can go around it," Learoyd explains.
In addition to increasing energy output, this improves the appearance as the silver wires aren't visible.
Another advantage, Heinrich says, is that "since we cut the cells into smaller areas, we can fill out special sizes more easily. You don't have to adhere to the regular pattern size."
Freesuns is an early adopter of matrix shingling technology in building-integrated PV. "We see it as a big opportunity for the future in terms of how we would make our tiles," Learoyd says.
What would also help the company is better software for automated design. This would speed up the design process, since each roofing job is unique.
Learoyd believes this would lower costs and give "the whole construction industry much more confidence in using the product".
Ten years after her own solar roof was installed, and despite the sector's setbacks, Learoyd remains optimistic.
She believes that for people with the means, it will eventually become standard to install a new roof with some sort of embedded solar. "It's just a no-brainer."

articles.headline: Pentagon confirms Fort Hood terrorist's firing squad execution will be livestreamed: 'Details will follow'
keyFacts: A War Department official confirmed that the military firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed.
Hasan was sentenced to death after being convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others at Fort Hood in 2009.
Scheduled for December 3, this will be the first U.S. military execution since 1961 and the first by firing squad since 1945.
body: The Pentagon confirmed to Fox News Digital on Thursday that the firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, allowing the public to witness the military's first execution in more than six decades.
"It will be livestreamed. Details will follow," a War Department official told Fox News Digital.
The execution is scheduled for Dec. 3 at Fort Hood, Texas.
FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD

Hasan, a former Army major, killed 13 people and wounded 32 others when he opened fire on unarmed soldiers and civilians after shouting "Allahu Akbar" at Fort Hood on Nov. 5, 2009. He was convicted in 2013 and sentenced to death for the massacre.

President Donald Trump approved the use of an Army firing squad, following War Secretary Pete Hegseth's recommendation. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell previously announced the decision on X, declaring, "Judgment day for Hasan has finally come."

If carried out, Hasan's execution would be the first by the U.S. military since 1961 and the first military execution by firing squad since 1945. Hasan remains on military death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

articles.headline: How to complete Taking Stock in ARC Raiders
keyFacts: The Taking Stock quest in ARC Raiders requires players to complete tasks across three separate maps.
Players must take photos of a sculpture in the Stella Montis Atrium and a Baron Husk on Spaceport.
Players must also ping a Bombardier on Dam Battlegrounds without needing to deal damage.
body: The Taking Stock quest there is a new objective to complete in ARC Raiders, and finishing all the tasks will help you get some really useful rewards. While we have the Pendola Pass map as the new entry, this quest will require you to visit Stella Montis and older maps.
Let’s find out how to complete all the tasks of this objective quickly.
Table of contents
ARC Raiders Taking Stock quest walkthrough On Stella Montis, take a photo of the sculpture in the Atrium
On Spaceport, take a photo of a Baron Husk
On Dam Battlegrounds, ping a Bombardier
ARC Raiders Taking Stock quest walkthrough
The Taking Stock quest has three main tasks, and you’ll have to visit three separate maps. You’ll also need to bring a camera with you because there will be few pictures to click.
On Stella Montis, take a photo of the sculpture in the Atrium

Screenshot and remix by Destructoid First, head to the marked location in the image above, and you will arrive in the Atrium. You will find the gigantic star-shaped sculpture right in the middle, and it is impossible to miss.
You simply need to equip your camera from the inventory and click a picture of it. This area has plenty of ARCs usually roaming the corridors, so you must be careful.
On Spaceport, take a photo of a Baron Husk

Screenshot and remix by Destructoid Baron Husks are gigantic remains of ARCs that lie dormant across the map. For this task, you have to snap a photo of at least one of them on the Stella Montis map. I have marked the two spots on the image above.
Typically, you will find one of these husks along the massive wall that separates the outer areas of Spaceport from the inner ones.
On Dam Battlegrounds, ping a Bombardier

Screenshot and remix by Destructoid This was an optional task, since you can also ping a Bastion on Buried City. Dam Battlegrounds, being the first map, has always been the easiest one to learn, and all I had to do was ping a bombardier. You do not need to put any kind of damage.

I have marked a couple of locations on the map above that will typically have a Bombardier. Their actual locations tend to be rather random. You can also try to find a metric or queen run happening on Dam Battlegrounds to make things easier.
