articles.headline: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
keyFacts: Mikel Arteta hopes resting Declan Rice during the international break will benefit the player before Saturday's match against Leeds.
Bournemouth player Alex Scott will be out of action for two months after suffering an injury on England duty.
Manchester City will face Liverpool as they resume Premier League play following a guilty verdict regarding legal issues.
body: Declan Rice’s future role in England’s midfield was questioned by Gary Lineker after Alex Scott’s impressive first senior international start in the 7-0 thrashing of Croatia. But the decision to withdraw from Thomas Tuchel’s squad in an attempt to manage his workload made sense after Rice had only three weeks off post-World Cup before returning to pre-season training. The 27-year-old has struggled with persistent back problems after suffering a hamstring injury last December and Mikel Arteta will hope that the rest has done Rice – who is thought to be close to agreeing a lucrative new contract at the Emirates – the world of good as they prepare to resume the defence of their Premier League title against Leeds on Saturday. Ed Aarons

Several Aston Villa players shone for their countries during the international window but one of those who stayed with the club may have made the biggest impression on Unai Emery. Villa’s remaining squad went to Spain for a mid-season training camp, including Alejandro Garnacho, whose last cap for Argentina was almost two years ago. Garnacho has been lesser-spotted in a Villa shirt, playing just 31 minutes as a substitute, but scored in both of Villa’s friendlies during the break, against Southampton and Sevilla. The 22-year-old, who joined Villa on loan from Chelsea in the summer with a conditional obligation, was an unused substitute for their past matches but is he now primed to affect games? Villa are hopeful Emery has unlocked Garnacho, who has struggled for form since leaving Manchester United. “Ready now!” Garnacho posted on social media last weekend and Villa will hope that is the case. Ben Fisher

With Eli Junior Kroupi, Amine Adli, Veljko Milosavljevic and Julián Araujo yet to feature this season due to injury, Marco Rose must have been tearing his remaining hair out upon learning Alex Scott got hurt on England duty and will be out of action for two months. Sitting 17th and still searching for their first league win, the German’s side squandered nine points from winning positions in four of their first five games – and it was the 23-year-old who was central in ensuring Bournemouth had those leads in the first place. With just 55 minutes of football behind him this season, it seems unlikely Alex Toth will get the nod to replace Scott when Bournemouth travel to Chelsea with the older, more experienced Ryan Christie available and in good form. But having forced his way into the Hungary starting lineup during the international break it would be no surprise to see the 20-year-old get more minutes with a view to being used far more often given his side’s gruelling schedule of nine matches in the next month. Barry Glendenning
Chelsea v Bournemouth, Saturday 3pm

Ipswich’s place in mid-table, their total of six points, came via victories over Sunderland and Crystal Palace. Gary O’Neil’s team were presented with a tough opening schedule, and while defeated by Manchester United, Liverpool and Arsenal, their manager has not allowed those reverses to dilute team spirit. Speaking to the media following the home defeat by Liverpool, O’Neil painted an ultra-positive picture that defied most observers’ view of a game beyond his team’s reach from the early stages. Thus far, a successful strategy, certainly by comparison to early season at winless Fulham. Like O’Neil, Álvaro Arbeloa is new to his job. An improved performance in the draw against United did not result in a victory Fulham deserved, though there were signs of the progressive, attacking football the arrival of the former Real Madrid interim promised. Much of the burden has fallen on Josh King, the teenager building on last year’s breakthrough season. John Brewin

Still in the Carabao Cup, with a Europa League campaign to negotiate and just four points acquired from their opening five Premier League excursions, the games are about to start coming thick and fast for a Sunderland side whose ability to cope with such a hectic schedule remains to be seen. Having lost Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey to hamstring injuries during the international break, Régis Le Bris will have to reshuffle his pack against a free-scoring Brighton side who make the 700-mile round trip to Wearside for their first game since embarrassing Arsenal three weeks ago. While Wilson Isidor will almost certainly deputise for Brobbey, Ballard’s centre-back berth will be filled by either Omar Alderete or Nordi Mukiele. Having shipped five last time out against Manchester City, a Sunderland defence that had looked conspicuously porous in the early stages of this season will need all their focus if they are to stop the gallop of a team that have already scored 16 goals. BG.

If “Dr Tottenham” is a thing, Manchester United possess their own healing powers for opponents. Self-harm is a factor too. They rolled out the welcome mat to Premier League newcomers Hull on opening day and Brighton were ushered back into a Carabao Cup tie. In United’s final game before the international break flagging Fulham were able to restore some faith, their goal via slapstick defending from Lisandro Martínez and Senne Lammens. Can Old Trafford, where fans will have regulatory matters at City to celebrate, lift the gloom for Tottenham? This season, like last season and the one before that, Spurs have assumed the mantle of crisis club, a status Michael Carrick’s January arrival temporarily removed from United. Lose to Tottenham, and the crisis prefix is likely to be reattached. Tottenham have done damage before. In September 2024, a 3-0 Spurs win at Old Trafford began Erik ten Hag’s hurtle towards the exit. Losing the Europa League final started Ruben Amorim’s downward spiral. Carrick beware? JB

All eyes will be on Oliver Glasner as he returns to Selhurst Park with Nottingham Forest on an afternoon that will be emotionally charged for both sets of supporters and in the boardroom. The Crystal Palace chair, Steve Parish, sought to defuse tensions last week when he urged fans to “buck the trend” by welcoming the manager who led the south London club to the first three major trophies in their history in the space of 12 months. “I would be mortified if he gets anything other than the roof blown off,” said Parish. But given the strength of feeling towards Forest and their owner, Evangelos Marinakis – who is still blamed by some for Palace’s demotion to the Conference League at the expense of Forest last season – many have still not forgiven Glasner for joining their rivals and could still make their feelings known when the Austrian takes his seat in the dugout before kick-off. EA

In Sergej Jakirovic and David Moyes, Hull City and Everton boast two of the more “pragmatic” managers in the Premier League. Renowned for their safety-first defensive styles, both teams are happy to surrender possession, rank among the top flight’s lowest sides in pass completion rates, and rely on rapid transitions and set pieces for a major share of their total expected goals. A game featuring two defences that pride themselves on their obduracy may well be settled by a well-delivered dead ball into a packed penalty area. While it may not be aesthetically pleasing, expect to see the massed ranks of defenders on both sides spending much of Sunday afternoon bracing themselves for rearguard action while peering towards the sky. The last time these sides met in the Premier League, Everton ran out easy 4-0 winners. A decade on, the aerial traffic is unlikely to be quite so one-way. BG

Manchester City resume playing under the darkest of clouds, with a visit to their greatest rivals of a golden period now shrouded by a guilty verdict. Five Premier League wins from five under Enzo Maresca had offered hopes of success in a post-Pep Guardiola era. The dial has since moved on what constitutes success for a club where minds are consumed by legal issues but the band must play on. Can Maresca summon a siege mentality? City lifted a treble, including the Champions League, when the 100-plus charges first came to public light in 2023. The Anfield crowd will readily remind City of the infamy their club faces down. That Guardiola’s now-disputed dominance came at the cost of Jürgen Klopp’s great team will add to the ire, and very probably the pyro greeting to Anfield. Cool heads may be required in the policing and on the field, to which a return to focusing on football may offer welcome relief. JB

International football’s incursions have curbed the adrenaline rush of Coventry’s win at Nottingham Forest and Jay Dasilva’s brilliant goal, his club’s first in the top division since 2001. That gave Frank Lampard foundations to build on, a blueprint, where Forest were allowed to blow themselves out before Dasilva’s strike came on the counter. It was Stephen Mfuni, 18, on loan from Manchester City, who starred in that rearguard effort on his Premier League debut. Coventry now seek a first Premier League goal at a stadium opened in 2005, after the club’s long decline had set in. Newcastle this week passed five years of the ownership of a consortium led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. There have been two seasons of Champions League football, a trophy lifted and yet a sense of unfulfilled promise. Matthias Jaissle is leading the second phase of a jagged development process, this season’s positive signs tempered by reverses such as the 4-1 defeat by Leeds, shows how far Coventry must travel. JB

articles.headline: President Trump awards Big Tech donors with nation’s highest science prizes
keyFacts: President Trump awarded the National Medal of Science and the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to six Big Tech leaders.
The awardees have donated nearly six billion dollars to efforts tied to Trump and his administration, according to The New Republic.
Satya Nadella received his medal right after the administration indefinitely suspended Microsoft from the H-1B program for skilled foreign workers.
body: On Thursday, at the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit, President Trump awarded Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD’s Lisa Su the National Medal of Science, the nation’s top science prize. Dell Technologies’ Michael Dell and Microsoft’s Satya Nadella also received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

Together, the awardees have donated nearly $6 billion to efforts tied to Trump and his administration, according to The New Republic. Alphabet and Microsoft, for example, donated to the president’s inauguration fund and White House ballroom. AMD gave to a pro-Trump Super PAC, and Michael and Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to help fund the Trump Accounts, the administration’s savings program for children.
Trump said the honorees had helped “pioneer an incredible future for America,” and that because of them, “we will always be on top. No one else can compete with us.”
Nadella received his medal right after the administration indefinitely suspended Microsoft from the H-1B program, which lets U.S. companies hire skilled foreign workers.

articles.headline: US plans livestream of execution by firing squad
keyFacts: Former US Army major Nidal Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3rd, Defense Department officials said.
Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in Texas.
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution will be public, and officials stated it will be livestreamed.
body: The United States’ execution of the Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed, anonymous officials from the Defense Department told the BBC and Associated Press. The planned execution of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army major convicted of killing 13 people at the Texas military base, was announced this week. He is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3rd at 2PM ET.
US plans livestream of execution by firing squad
The planned execution of Nidal Hasan will be ‘public,’ Pete Hegseth said in an interview.
The Verge contacted YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Meta, Rumble, and Kick to ask if they plan to allow the livestream to be aired on their platforms. None responded before publication.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in an interview with Real America’s Voice.

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo is a ‘total narcissist’ but could win civil war against Jorge Jesus
keyFacts: Cristiano Ronaldo left the Portugal national team camp after accusing manager Jorge Jesus of breaking promises regarding his playing time.
Football expert Eric Krakauer said the Portuguese Football Federation may prioritize Ronaldo over Jesus because Ronaldo brings in significant revenue.
Krakauer predicted the situation will drag on and the federation might decide Ronaldo is worth more than Jesus.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo has been called a ‘total narcissist’ amid his ongoing battle with Jorge Jesus, but the player could have the last laugh.
That is according to Portuguese football expert Eric Krakauer, who feels Ronaldo’s importance has potential to outweigh that of the recently appointed Jesus’.
Ronaldo is Portugal’s greatest player, but his international career is all ending horribly Getty
The 41-year-old started the 1-0 win over Wales during this international break, but he was an unused substitute in the following game against Norway and was sent out to warm up.
Ronaldo then left the camp and played no part in the rest of the matches, which Portugal won.
Jesus has a 100 per cent record as Portugal’s manager, but that might not be enough to save him.
Joining Kick Off , Krakauer said: “The tarnishing of his reputation is very, very sad for him and for the country because he put Portugal on the map.
“The complicated situation is that the Portuguese Football Federation is more concerned with the amount of money it has in its coffers rather than the success of the national team.
“That is one of the reasons they didn’t put Roberto Martinez under any pressure to sideline Ronaldo in the World Cup, even though playing him was essentially sacrificing their success.

“Ronaldo brings a tremendous amount of money to the Portuguese Football Federation, so they understand that without him, they aren’t going to have the same sort of income. He is essentially a cash cow, and they are not ready to part ways with that money.
“So, I see this dragging on for a while, and hopefully, Jorge Jesus isn’t the sacrificial lamb because the federation might decide that Ronaldo is worth a lot more than Jesus.”
And Krakauer added that he believes Ronaldo is a ‘total narcissist’ for comparing himself to Diego Maradona and Pele and then asking the manager to read out some points at a press conference.

“He also compared himself with Pele and Maradona. Oh, don’t. Right, which, you know, he can be in that conversation, maybe, but I think it takes a total narcissist. And I’m sorry to say this about a player that I love. It takes a narcissist to write that down,”Krakauer added.
Jesus has decided that Ronaldo will be a bit-part player in his team AFP
Ronaldo’s statement
After leaving the camp, Ronaldo revealed that he would explain everything, and he did in a very long statement, accusing Jesus of breaking promises to him.

Part of it read as follows: “This is the truth on what has happened with Jorge Jesus. As I promised, I decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances surrounding the last training camp of the national team.

“I told the President of the Federation that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice to retire. That is why, on the day the current head coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results are confirming. A few days later I received a first contact from the new national team coach saying he would like to meet me in person.

“He presented me, right there, with a plan for my participation. He told me I would play the first match and the last one, and that for reasons of physical management he would always make three to four changes per match.

“At that point he raised the possibility of me not travelling with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He proposed that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then rejoin before the match at the Dragao.

“I refused this proposal immediately. It seemed obvious to me that I could not accept it. It was not because I would not play the matches abroad that I would stop captaining our team. That privilege of staying in Portugal would not be a good example. The coach ended up agreeing with my analysis.
“At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, an assistant to the coach came to the table where the group was having lunch and informed me that the coach wanted to speak to me.
Ronaldo’s decline on the international stage has been clear for all to see Getty

“To my absolute surprise, the coach asked me if I was fit to play 30 minutes. I was fully focused on my physical recovery, integrated with my teammates as always, and thinking that I would not play that day. Without any problem.
“This request was something outside my physical recovery and training plan — because I was only going to play on the 4th at the Dragao — but of course I said yes.

“He replied that I should then be ready because I would play 30 minutes. The rest everyone knows. I warmed up from half-time, watched the minutes go by, and was not called. The coach had broken his word to me.”
Ronaldo’s decline
During the 2026 World Cup, Ronaldo scored in his sixth edition of the tournament, but Portugal crashed out early on.
This despite them having a team full of world-class players, and it was the same in the 2024 European Championships as well.
And Krakauer believes that the Ronaldo downfall has been happening for a while and has contributed to those failures.

He said: “It’s a tragic affair in a football sense that Portugal’s greatest player is basically walking out on his team and blemishing what was until recently, an unblemishable legacy with international football.
“But there is no doubt once you take everything into account, he’s essentially orchestrated his own demise.
“He’s had the power for nearly two decades, but over the last four or five years, the conversation hasn’t been about Ronaldo and his supporting cast.

“Different players have become more prominent and Ronaldo was declining, though, he could never seem to accept that, starting in 2022 when Fernando Santos decided to bench him for Goncalo Ramos because he believed that Ronaldo was a detriment to the team.
“That doesn’t mean he didn’t have a part to play, but he wasn’t physically able to offer the team what they needed, which was a pressing forward.
“It seemed as if we were going to see Ronaldo being phased out. Unfortunately, Roberto Martinez was hired, and he decided to indulge his superstar.
“He said that no one could take his place in the XI, and in Euro 2024 and the World Cup, it was obvious he was a detriment except to Ronaldo.”

articles.headline: No one wants to be “Data Center Dave”
keyFacts: Bipartisan voter backlash against artificial intelligence and data centers is increasingly influencing political campaigns across the United States.
Candidates from both major parties are attempting to distance themselves from data centers in several high-profile midterm races.
Americans will vote in these races in less than four weeks, but very few voters name data centers as their top issue.
body: Amazon Web Services data center in Stone Ridge, Virginia. | Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .
As far as political slurs go, this one is pretty tepid: “Meet Data Center Dave Crowley,” intones the stern-voiced narrator of a recent Tom Tiffany campaign ad .

Tiffany, a Republican, and Crowley, a Democrat, are both running for governor of Wisconsin. And in this very tight race, as in dozens of midterm contests across the country, voters’ growing animus toward AI could potentially make a real difference .

In less than four weeks, Americans will head to the polls to decide which party controls Congress, along with a slew of state and local offices. The stakes are arguably, unusually high: Voters will choose whether to check the power of a president who has bulldozed over historical limits and launched an unpopular war that has worsened a cost-of-living crisis.

As we count down to that momentous and potentially messy day, I’m partnering with my colleague Astead Herndon and Vox’s The Midterms, Actually team for weekly editions on the biggest issues shaping the midterms. We’re breaking down one issue each week and suggesting further reading and races to watch in November.

Last week, we tackled the dual identity crises that both parties have suffered since 2024 . And this week, we’re digging into the dramatic bipartisan backlash to AI and data centers. One analyst recently told NPR the issue “upended politics as we know it.” But it’s less clear how that’ll play out in November’s contests.
Go a little deeper
View Link

There was a time not so long ago when “Data Center Dave” might be a neutral nickname for the well-meaning IT guy at work. Then Americans soured on AI and the hulking, cavernous warehouses that supply its computing power.

The hostility crosses geography and party lines. At first, opponents focused on noise, water use, and energy costs — quality-of-life concerns for nearby residents. But increasingly, even voters far from these projects grew leery of them.

Too often, the public got little say in where data centers were built and on what terms. And as Vox’s Marina Bolotnikova reported over the summer, the construction boom gradually became a stand-in for broader fears about artificial intelligence . Would AI cause mass unemployment (…or worse, mass extinction)? Would it widen the gap between rich and poor? And do politicians cater to business interests over the needs of ordinary people ?
Without clear answers to those questions — let alone a rigorous plan to address AI’s fallout — many voters channeled their unease into stopping, or slowing, data center development.

Candidates have reacted by “falling over themselves to sound tough on data centers,” Washington Post data reporter Jeremy Merrill recently told Vox’s Noel King. He analyzed thousands of social media posts and newsletters to see how elected officials are talking about data centers, and the answer is: not positively!

Some candidates in high-profile midterm races have backed policies that would keep data centers from raising household energy bills. Others have called for ending the facilities’ tax breaks and subsidies or requiring public notice before new construction. Strikingly, both Republicans and Democrats have supported these types of proposals … and both Republicans and Democrats have sought to tar their opponents as “Data Center Daves” of one kind or another .

I asked my colleague Andrew Prokop, who covers politics, if many races will actually turn on this. “Data centers have been a major theme in several races, particularly governor’s races where one of the candidates has taken past pro-data center positions,” he said.

But even when voters say they oppose data centers, very few list the issue among the most important concerns determining how they cast their ballots. In Ohio, for instance — a hub for both data-center development and the grassroots movement opposing it — only 3 percent of voters named data centers as the top issue driving their vote. And that’s the highest share in the entire nation.

Andrew points to the Democratic gubernatorial primary in Wisconsin, where “Data Center Dave” triumphed over Francesca Hong, an outspoken data center critic. “That just goes to show that data centers don’t necessarily crowd out everything else,” Andrew said.
Still…that’s just one race. And voters’ hatred of data centers has only grown since.
➨ Races to watch:
Wisconsin governor’s race, where both candidates have attempted to distance themselves from data centers without embracing an actual ban;
Texas governor’s race, where Republican Governor Greg Abbott has hastily retreated from his previous, pro-data-center position;
Ohio Senate race, where Democrat Sherrod Brown has hammered incumbent Republican Jon Husted over his past votes for data center development.
➨ More from Vox:
Data centers could actually be good for your hometown
Americans don’t know how to fight AI. So they’re fighting data centers.
The real reason voters hate data centers so much

➨ Get better at being alone with your thoughts. According to one oft-cited study from 2014, many people would rather give themselves electric shocks than spend a few minutes alone with nothing to do. But being alone with your thoughts is good for you ! You can practice by making a list of topics to ponder and parking your phone in another room. Then see what kind of cogitation surfaces for you.

articles.headline: US disrupts Chinese hacking tools as 7 govts warn of PRC spies stealing sensitive data worldwide
keyFacts: The FBI seized seven web domains linked to hacking tools operated by Chinese security firm Integrity Technology Group.
Seven international governments warned that Chinese state-backed hackers used these tools to target global critical infrastructure and steal sensitive data.
Based on this cyber activity, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added five vulnerabilities to its known exploited catalog.
body: The FBI announced that it has seized seven web domains linked to hacking tools allegedly operated by a Chinese security firm called Integrity Technology Group and used by Beijing-backed cyber operatives to scan a South Carolina power company's network and other critical infrastructure systems for vulnerabilities. In a subsequent advisory, the FBI and other government agencies in the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain warned that Chinese government-linked attackers, enabled by Integrity Tech, are using botnets, malware, and other intrusion tools to target organizations worldwide and steal sensitive data, including from US critical infrastructure networks. “These actors exploit vulnerabilities by using scanning tools, cross-site scripting attacks, and password spraying on Microsoft Exchange servers, while establishing persistence through VPN software and exfiltrating emails and credentials using scripts,” according to the security alert. Based on this activity, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added five CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog: CVE-2015-3306 CVE-2015-5477 CVE-2016-3081 CVE-2021-3199 CVE-2023-22894 The court-authorized seizures are the latest in a long series of US law-enforcement attempts to disrupt a Beijing-backed cybercrew called Flax Typhoon and shut down its botnet. From 2021 until its disruption, Flax Typhoon allegedly used a version of this Mirai-based botnet to infect internet-connected devices with malware, scan networks for vulnerabilities, and launch additional cyberattacks, all while hiding the PRC government hackers’ true IP addresses and physical location. The feds allege Integrity Tech developed the botnet and a vulnerability scanner called Microscan, and operated a post-compromise tool called FishHub. The latter allegedly downloaded additional malware to the phishing victims’ networks and stole sensitive data. Court documents, unsealed on Thursday, allege Integrity Tech has contracts with the PRC government, and the feds have long linked Flax Typhoon to the private firm. “Flax Typhoon actors conducted successful computer intrusions against multiple victim entities which had been scanned using the Microscan tool,” according to the court documents. Victims include a university in Hsinchu, Taiwan, that Flax Typhoon compromised in March 2023, and a second university in Puli Township, Taiwan breached in August 2022. “On or about April 26, 2022, and on or about December 29, 2022, Flax Typhoon actors also used the Microscan tool to scan for vulnerabilities on the networks of a U.S. power company based in South Carolina, a multi-national Non-Governmental Organization, Japanese and Polish airports, and at least two Taiwanese critical infrastructure companies in the natural gas and power sectors,” the documents allege. Integrity Tech accessed Microscan through one of the seized domains, c0cc[.]cc. Meanwhile, five of the seized domains, 98aicai[.]com, 98aicode[.]com, outlook3650[.]com, youtubecard[.]com, and linkedinns[.]net, delivered the FishHub malware as recently as March, and infected about 20 Taiwanese universities. “Based on my training and experience I believe the tool was named FishHub because it facilitated phishing activity,” FBI special agent Adam James said in a seizure warrant affidavit. After FishHub downloaded a file onto victims' computers, that file used the five domains to retrieve additional malicious programs and code. The malware created a file listing, searched for specific files, compressed documents, and then exfiltrated the selected files to an attacker-controlled server. This gave Flax Typhoon remote access to compromised networks. In September 2024, the FBI said Integrity Tech and Flax Typhoon tore down their 260,000-device botnet after the FBI and its international pals went after them. As recently as this year, however, both private sector security researchers and Western governments warned that Chinese hackers continue to turn compromised routers and IoT devices into botnets and break into critical networks. In February, operational technology (OT) security provider Dragos said China’s state-sponsored spies haven't let up on their attempts to compromise America's critical infrastructure, and this includes a group whose activity overlaps with Flax Typhoon. This group focuses on gaining long-term access to OT engineering workstations and exfiltrating operational files, and it targets manufacturing, defense, automotive, electric power, oil and gas, and government organizations across the US, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region. In April, a 10-country joint advisory warned that basically every Chinese “Typhoon” group is using botnets “strategically, and at scale.” Some of these covert networks are built and maintained by Chinese infosec companies including Integrity Tech, which also controlled and managed the so-called Raptor Train network, the alert said. In late August, the FBI said that it had disrupted a different botnet and seized domains associated with two platforms that Chinese government-backed operatives allegedly used to target NASA, the US Senate, the Department of Energy, and several other government agencies and critical networks. The DOJ subsequently clarified that not all the named organizations had been compromised.®

articles.headline: You can now sign up to playtest the genre-bending Pony Island 2: Panda Circus, and while you're at it the original is free for a few days too
keyFacts: Players can now sign up for the playtest of Pony Island 2: Panda Circus on Steam, according to the article.
The original Pony Island game is available for free on Steam until October 12th.
Developer Daniel Mullins has scheduled the release of Pony Island 2: Panda Circus for April 27th, 2027.
body: I love an everything seasoning video game. You know, the kind of game where it's five different genres at once, somehow, all of which builds into one cohesive vision? It's not an easy thing to pull off, but Daniel Mullins seems to be quite good at it, as evidenced by Inscryption, and as suggested by the upcoming Pony Island 2: Panda Circus. Which, by the way, now has a playtest you can sign up for.

A new trailer for Pony Island 2: Panda Circus dropped during the latest Triple-i Initiative, showing off more of the game and its genre-bending ways in action. You can check that out below for a taste. The trailer's main purpose was to inform you of that aforementioned playtest; signing up is easy, all you have to do is head to the puzzle horror's Steam page and mark yourself as interested in the playtest. Not sure if there's guaranteed entry for everyone that signs up, but hey ho, clicking a couple of buttons won't harm you (I cannot be held responsible if clicking a couple of buttons does harm you).

If that doesn't work, there's some other good news: the original Pony Island is available to pick up on Steam completely for free! All you have to do is add it to your account before October 12th, and it's yours forever. Certainly a clever way to get folks interested in a sequel to a game that's over 10 years old (and a way to get people to play said game at all, too). The original Pony Island is certainly a bit simpler than its impending followup, but hey, old ain't bad!

Panda Circus does look a touch more involved. There is some of that pony riding sidescrolling business going on, but there's also some kind of 3D world to explore where you shoot a bow and arrow, a bullet heaven-esque looking element, some kind of borderline dungeon crawlery/Inscryptiony looking bit with bears asking if you slept at all, minigames including one where you have to make clowns stand up, a Pac-Man rip-off, FMV cutscenes, the list goes on! And if any of this is of interest, even if you don't make it into the playtest, you don't have too long to wait, as the game is due out April 27th, 2027.

articles.headline: This ‘Mind-Reading’ AI Is a Wiz at Figuring Out What You See
keyFacts: Israeli scientists developed an AI model called Brain-IT that reconstructs images people see by analyzing their fMRI brain scans.
Researchers said the technology could help people with communication disabilities and requires much less training data than existing models.
The team next wants to test if they can reconstruct auditory information and eventually decode dreams, researchers said.
body: Israeli scientists have devised an AI model that can reconstruct and even predict what people are seeing with startling accuracy, likening the results to mind reading.

Their work still exists largely in lab settings, though the researchers are hopeful that advances down the line could be extended even as far as reading people’s dreams. More immediately, the technology could have potential for medical purposes, like helping people communicate who otherwise can’t due to injury or disability.

The AI model, called Brain-IT, was developed by professor Michal Irani and fellow researchers at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel. They’ve documented their work on GitHub and in a paper presented at a scientific conference earlier this year.
More from CNET

Brain-IT takes advantage of the thing that AI is best at, which is pattern recognition. It takes in data from functional MRI brain scans, which track changes in blood flow and oxygen in the brain to measure brain activity, and then uses that data to recreate the images the person was thinking about when the scans took place.
It also works in reverse, predicting what a brain scan would look like if shown a specific image.
According to Irani, other AI models can translate brain activity into images and preserve the general vibe of an image.

“However, they tend to make mistakes in basic features such as composition and color,” Irani said in a statement. “The new model we developed outperforms them in reconstructing both the content of the image and its details.”
Brain-IT is also substantially faster. The researchers say that it needs only 1 hour of fMRI data from a new subject to match the results achieved by other methods trained on 40 hours of recording.
How does the Brain-IT AI model work?

The Weizmann Institute researchers trained the AI model on thousands of brain scans from the publicly available Natural Scenes Dataset that came from eight volunteers who were told to look at specific images while they were being scanned. This allowed the AI to identify patterns in brain activity.

The researchers noted that different regions of the brain light up on scans when people think about specific things and identified 128 “functional regions.” For example, Irani said, some regions light up in scans when someone looks at food and others when a person views sports. These patterns helped the AI figure out what the person being scanned was witnessing.

Some of these regions were already known by neuroscientists. Research has shown that dogs’ brains light up like Christmas trees in the presence of their owners and that dogs can differentiate between a human’s facial expressions. It’s also been observed that humans use the same neurons in recalling an image as they do looking at them.

As impressive as Brain-IT is, it’s also quite limited. It can currently only generate images from fMRI brain scans. This takes time and requires a person to willingly put themselves into an MRI machine.
Irani and other scientists are also looking into whether a simpler EEG device could deliver similar results more easily, according to MIT Technology Review.

So is it mind reading? Not really — nothing in this technology is capturing thoughts, memory or language. What the Weizmann Institute researchers have built is essentially a more efficient and reliable method of reconstructing a scene based on the brain activity of the person viewing it.
In an interview with MIT Technology Review, Irani acknowledged that “mind-reading” is a “cute, jazzy name.”
Irani and her team now want to see if they can achieve similar results with auditory information.
Beyond that lies a more mysterious realm: dreams. That, Irani said in a statement, would require conquering the challenges of decoding video.

“Dozens of images change every second while an fMRI scan takes about two minutes,” she said. “If we overcome all these obstacles, it’s possible that in the future, we may even be able to read dreams.”

articles.headline: Damn, This GTA 6 Screenshot Looks So Good People Don’t Believe It’s Real
keyFacts: Rockstar Games released new screenshots for Grand Theft Auto 6, including a nighttime street scene that prompted skepticism from fans regarding its graphical quality.
Digital Foundry expert Oliver Mackenzie stated that Rockstar may have used a debug tool or a PS5 Pro devkit to capture the high-resolution image.
Mackenzie noted visual faults in the image, such as dithering and missing shadows, that resemble typical console game settings.
body: Earlier today, Rockstar Games shared new information about the music and radio stations that will appear in Grand Theft Auto 6.Â Included with that news were a few new screenshots. And one particular screenshot featuring cars on a rainy street at night has got people freaking out and wondering if GTA 6 will actually look like this on consoles. And the answer is, yeah, probably. Mostly.

On October 8, Rockstar revealed that numerous famous musicians, including Bad Bunny, would host some of the radio stations in GTA 6. We also got our first official confirmation of some of these stations and what kinds of music they’ll play, and learned that you’ll be able to listen to all of them on foot via your phone. But on the website sharing all this info, a background screenshot of GTA 6 caught many people’s attention, including my own. Here’s a direct link to a super high-res version of it.Â

In the screenshot, we can spot a few different cars and people on a rainy street somewhere in the heart of Vice City at night. In the background, the neon lights of the Ocean View Hotel light up the buildings and wet pavement. And in the puddles, you can spot reflections of cars and other parts of the environment. It’s truly impressive, and fans online are freaking out over how good it looks while others are worried it might not be real or is doctored to look better than anything the actual game can produce when running on a PS5 in November.
“Ain’t no way that first screenshot is real; it looks so good,” replied one person on social media.
“Thought these were renders, but actual shots?” asked another user.

Digital Foundry’s Oliver Mackenzie weighed in on the matter when pinged by GTA content creator Ben VideoTech, and suggested that Rockstar may be using some sort of debug photo mode that would allow them to turn up resolution and settings to make the shot look as good as possible. However, as pointed out by Mackenzie, if you look at the screenshot closely, you can start to notice some visual faults that suggest it could be a shot captured from the game running on PS5 Pro. But “it’s not really possible to tell.”

It's not perfect though. The reflections in the mid-field on a kind of semi-gloss road and sidewalk surface are pretty messy looking and seem indicative of something close to console settings. pic.twitter.com/sfvoZpimpc
— Oliver Mackenzie (@oliemack) October 8, 2026

For example, reflections further back in the image show obvious dithering, something we see all the time on reflections in most console games in 2026. You can also spot that shadows aren’t being drawn under pedestrians in the far distance. And if you look really far in the background and zoom in a lot, you can even spot what look like lower-poly people standing around.

In the past, Rockstar has generally used real, in-game and in-engine footage and screenshots of its upcoming games for marketing screenshots and trailers. I remember when GTA V was coming out, people looked at screenshots of the game and swore Rockstar was using touched-up images or running the game on high settings on PC. However, looking back at GTA V‘s Xbox 360 screenshots in 2026, it’s very clear these were taken in the game. Perhaps captured using a debug tool that let Rockstar turn up some settings and add some extra lights and poses, but GTA V‘s pre-release shots are very representative of what the game looked like on Xbox 360 and PS3. This is true of other Rockstar titles, too, like Red Dead, Bully, and Max Payne 3.Â

I think what’s likely happened here is that Rockstar is running the game on a PS5 Pro devkit and is using some sort of debug menu to take a super-crisp screenshot of the game at its highest possible resolution. So while the final game might rarely look this perfect and clean, I do think that, yeah, GTA 6 is going to look incredible at night on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X. As for Xbox Series S, well, good luck, my friends.

articles.headline: Why a 21-year-old coder finally ported the real P.T. to PC: 'That something so influential could eventually become unplayable never sat right with me'
keyFacts: Programmer Lorean Xavier has released a native PC port of Hideo Kojima's delisted horror game P.T. for Windows and Linux.
The native client requires a dumped copy of the original game to function, allowing Xavier to add modern graphical features and mod support.
Dataminer Lance McDonald stated that the project appears to be a one-to-one port of the entire codebase.
body: One of the most beloved horror games (demos?) of all time is finally free from the shackles of the PS4. Hideo Kojima's P.T. has been natively ported to PC by programmer Lorean Xavier, who made the project public this week. Not an emulator nor a remake, the native PC client does not contain any copyrighted materials—it requires a dumped copy of P.T. to function—but instead translates the original code into something that'll run on Windows and Linux.

That distinction not only sidesteps potential corporate scrutiny, but also allows Xavier to add modern graphical features and mod support to the PC version. It's an impressive effort that, according to the creator, has been in the works since 2024.

"I wanted to make the version of P.T. that my younger self always wished existed," Xavier, 21, told PC Gamer over email. "My attachment to the game goes all the way back to my childhood. I remember watching videos of it on my phone, wishing I could experience it myself. I didn't have a PS4, so playing the original was never really an option for me. I never imagined back then that I'd eventually be the one bringing it to PC."

The window to play P.T. "legitimately" was famously brief. Kojima surprise-dropped P.T. on the PlayStation Network in 2014 as a "playable teaser" for the Silent Hills reboot he was making with Guillermo Del Toro. When Kojima and Konami had a falling out, Silent Hills was canceled and P.T. got caught in the breakup, being delisted in early 2015. The horror classic has persisted only through emulation and preserved PS4 hard drives—until now.
"The idea that something so influential could eventually become practically unplayable never sat right with me," Xavier added.

"There have been several PC remakes over the years, and I appreciate that people tried to preserve the experience, but none of them ever really satisfied me," Xavier said. "Something always felt off, whether it was the lighting, the atmosphere, the interactions, or the way certain events played out. They could resemble P.T. visually, but they never truly felt like the original to me.

"And that's exactly why I wanted to do this differently. I didn't want to make another interpretation of P.T. or recreate it approximately in another engine. I wanted the actual experience, with its original assets, sounds, animations, and behavior, running natively on PC."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
While the project is "not a modified version or fork of [PS4 emulator] shadPS4," the emulated version was an "extremely valuable" reference to compare the original game's behavior to the port.

We're in weird and wild times for the recompilation scene as gen AI has accelerated the creation of console-to-PC ports, often with janky, hastily-vibecoded results that make good preservation more difficult. Xavier is open about using AI in his workflow, but believes it's no replacement for "actually knowing what you're doing."

"I think there's an important distinction between using AI as a development tool and blindly relying on it to create an entire project you don't understand. In my case, I use AI to help with debugging, identifying issues, testing code, and working through problems when I get stuck. It can be incredibly useful for accelerating that process, especially when you're working alone on something this complicated.

"But I'm still the one responsible for the architecture, the implementation decisions, writing and reviewing the code, and understanding how the different systems fit together. My years of experience with reverse engineering and P.T. are what allow me to direct that process in the first place."

In terms of faithfulness, the port has the seal of approval from at least one person who would know: Lance McDonald, the Australian creator who datamined P.T. and discovered many of its secrets back in the day, is impressed by what he reckons is a "1:1 port of the entire codebase."
You can check out the "PT-PC" project for yourself on GitHub.

Before freelancing, he spent most of high school and all of college writing at small gaming sites that didn't pay him. He's very happy to have a real job now. Morgan is a beat writer following the latest and greatest shooters and the communities that play them. He also writes general news, reviews, features, the occasional guide, and bad jokes in Slack. articles.headline: Maresca says 'feeling is fantastic' among Man City squad
keyFacts: Manchester City was found guilty of most of the 115 Premier League charges regarding disguised funding, and the club has launched an appeal.
Head coach Enzo Maresca said his players are focused on their upcoming match against Liverpool and are not worried about the club's crisis.
Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner urged a quick final verdict to protect the integrity of the Premier League.
body: - Published

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca says the "feeling is fantastic" among his players and they "don't care too much about the noise" surrounding the club after it was found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against it by the Premier League.

The club's international players returned to training on Thursday, nine days after the Premier League published a damning report that stated the club had used "sham" contracts to disguise secret funding of more than Â£830m.

BBC Sport reported this week that Maresca would address the players upon their return to domestic duty after news of the verdict broke while the majority of the squad were away with their respective nations.

It is understood the City head coach asked his players not to allow the crisis that has engulfed the club to affect their attitude and focus as the Premier League campaign gets back under way this weekend.
"The feeling is fantastic, to be honest," Maresca said in an in-house interview when asked about the mood among his squad prior to their trip to face Liverpool on Sunday (16:30 BST).
"The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league. The players are just focused on that.
"They know what we can control is the football side - they are not worried at all about different things.

"They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield."
Maresca added he felt "calm" and his squad trusts the club "completely".
City have launched an appeal and have publicly maintained their innocence.
The private communication to those with links to the playing staff at City has been equally as emphatic, it is understood.

Speaking to Sky Sports, striker Erling Haaland echoed his manager's sentiments, saying: "I care a lot about this place. I spent my first four years here, it's a special place for us. I care a lot about City and the fans. I am a fan myself. I feel with them.

"The fans will have a good time on Sunday - we have to stick together. We have to stay with each other and stay positive. No matter what happens in life, we always have to smile. Stay positive, look ahead, and try to win football games and enjoy the situation.
"We have to stick together and spread the love to each other. Enjoy the ride and smile."
What have other Premier League managers said?
As Premier League football returns following a three-week hiatus, managers of rival clubs can expect to be asked to comment on the City verdict during their compulsory pre-match press conferences.
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner will face the media on Friday but told reporters earlier in the week he hopes the process is completed "as soon as possible".

Glasner joined Forest from Crystal Palace in the summer and cited his experience of the latter's demotion from the Europa League to the Conference League in 2025 after the club breached multi-club ownership rules.
"Let's wait until the final verdict is spoken, but my wish is just that this is quick," Glasner said.

"Because we didn't know with Palace if we were in the Europa League or Conference League and then it was 'you will hear on Thursday' and then that became Monday, because it was always delayed. Then we got the final verdict 10 days before the Conference League started.
"That's why I think this must be [completed] as soon as possible.
"There is still damage for the Premier League, not just in England. It's a big topic all over the world, especially in Europe.
"The most important thing is the integrity of the league because as soon as the fans can't trust it, they won't watch it any more."
Some manager news conferences were held on Thursday and Leeds head coach Daniel Farke and Newcastle's Matthias Jaissle both steered clear of commenting at length on the matter.
It is understood a number of clubs have already taken a clear stance for their managers not to comment.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard - who played for City in the 2014-15 season - said the players will not feel they have lost their titles even if the club is stripped of them because it is part of their personal history.
City have yet to be punished but BBC Sport has been told there has been little appetite from within the Premier League - both the organisation and its clubs - for past titles to be taken from them.
"I have titles and I don't have my titles hanging on my wall at home, I have them in my head," said Lampard, who won the Premier League three times with Chelsea.
"You are competing against the best in the Premier League and a lot of things are out of [your] control but you are competing against the best and they're very hard to win.

"So I think it would be very hard to take someone's title away as a player individually as they should be in your head as opposed to in a beautiful glass cabinet or whatever. I know there are some who do that."
Lampard made 38 appearances and scored eight goals when he joined City in 2014 after 13 years at Chelsea.

articles.headline: R.I.P. Margaret Hamilton, whose code saved the Apollo 11 Moon landing
keyFacts: Margaret Hamilton, who led the development of NASA's Apollo onboard flight software, died last week at the age of 90.
Hamilton coined the term "software engineering" and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016.
Hamilton also programmed the computer that MIT mathematician Edward Lorenz used to construct his mathematical weather model.
body: Margaret Hamilton, who coined the term “software engineering” and led the development of onboard flight software for NASA’s Apollo program in the 1960s, died last week at the age of 90. A recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016, Hamilton was also immortalized as a LEGO minifig the following year—part of the “Women of NASA” set that also included astronauts Mae Jemison and Sally Ride.

“To say Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer—to say she was ahead of her time—would be a dramatic understatement. She was a software engineer at a time when that field was in its infancy, and she not only developed advanced code herself but also led a team in using that nascent technology to develop one of the most complex systems humanity had ever achieved,” said Olivier de Weck, interim head of the MIT Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics. “The Apollo program still stands as one of our greatest testaments to the power of collaboration, ingenuity, and engineering, and Hamilton was a fundamental contributor to that program’s success.”

Born in 1936 in Paoli, Indiana, Hamilton graduated from Earlham College in 1958 with a degree in mathematics and a minor in philosophy—the latter a nod to her father (a poet) and grandfather (a headmaster). She married her first husband, James Cox Hamilton, that same year. The plan was for her to work until he finished his law degree, after which he would support her through graduate school to earn a PhD in mathematics.

She ended up working for Edward Lorenz, the MIT mathematician who set out to construct a mathematical model of the weather using a set of differential equations representing changes in temperature, pressure, wind velocity, and the like. You’ve probably heard the famous story of how Lorenz kept a continuous simulation running on his LGP-30 computer, and of that fateful 1961 day when he realized that even small differences in starting values could lead to very different outcomes—a sensitivity to initial conditions that is a hallmark of chaos theory, along with strange attractors. You might not have known that it was Hamilton who was responsible for programming the LGP-30.
